correctness.rationale: Existing directed cycles cannot acquire new edges in an extending bijection, so an even one is fatal on every superset. The only free arrows pair the terminals and initials of distinguished open paths (an isolated vertex counts as both), specifying a permutation of paths. A resulting cycle has odd vertex length precisely when it contains an odd number of odd paths. Deleting the even objects leaves an odd-cycle permutation on u objects, and reinserting v labelled even objects in ordered lists after the u odd objects gives v! binom(u+v-1,v) choices per base permutation. The known odd-cycle EGF, or the labelled cycle construction in the frozen proof, then gives the displayed integer count and series. With no odd objects there are no nonempty admissible cycles; an empty path set is the unique completion if the existing cycles are odd. Adding one specified isolated point in the obstructed open-path case forces a single path-cycle with the point and all v even paths, giving v! and proving minimality. An independent enumeration agreed on all 36 coloured profiles of total size at most 7; it did not use the supplied checker. The proof, not the test, covers arbitrary finite sets and does not concern simultaneous extensions.

evidence: Etidadialiabadi–Gao concern qualitative extensions of families on finite supersets, including a cyclic-fundamental-group case. The coloured-permutation citation concerns no monochromatic cycles by title; the full text was not obtained.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Qualitative extension theorems do not supply fixed-set multiplicity or one-point sharpness. Excluding monochromatic cycles is a different local restriction: here an all-odd singleton is permitted and a mixed cycle with two odd objects is forbidden.

evidence: The known EGF is A(z)=(1+z)(1-z^2)^(-1/2). A list of even labels after each odd label gives the bivariate substitution z=x/(1-y).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The substitution gives the displayed square root mechanically; the ordered-gap factor is v! binom(u+v-1,v) and gives the binomial closed form. At u=1 that factor is exactly v! and the empty/even cases follow from the same parity test. No additional extension machinery or new enumerative identity is required.
searches: OEIS A000246 exact EGF; Etidadialiabadi–Gao cited odd-extension theorem

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Match each exposed path terminal to an exposed path initial to get the equivalent coloured-permutation problem. Erasing even objects recovers the ordinary odd-cycle problem; insert them after odd objects in ordered gap lists to recover all completions uniquely.
